root_cause.text: The function `gss_read_proxy_verf` unconditionally calls `memcpy(page_address(in_token->pages[0]), ...)` without first verifying that `length > 0`, leading to a NULL pointer dereference when a zero-length `gss_token` results in `pages == 0` and `in_token->pages[0]` being NULL.
root_cause.evidence: CVE description states "A zero length gss_token results in pages == 0 and in_token->pages[0] is NULL. The code unconditionally evaluates page_address(in_token->pages[0]) for the initial memcpy, which can dereference NULL even when the copy length is 0." The patch fixes this by guarding the memcpy with a length check.

When inlen=0, pages=0, so kcalloc(0, ...) may succeed but the array has no elements.
